name: Orthodox Marxism
summary: Orthodox Marxism is the systematized Marxism of the Second International, chiefly Karl Kautsky's, which treats historical materialism as a science showing that capitalism will fall through its internal contradictions and give way to socialism. It pursues this through an independent mass workers' party that uses unions, universal suffrage and parliament, holds that history cannot be hurried, and rejects both Bernstein's revisionism and, in Kautsky's later writing, Bolshevik dictatorship.
scope: The Second International orthodoxy of Kautsky (the Erfurt Program commentary of 1892 and The Dictatorship of the Proletariat, 1918), Plekhanov and the pre-1914 SPD, and Lukacs's definition of orthodoxy as method. It excludes Leninism, Stalinism, Maoism, Western Marxism and impossibilist or anti-revisionist offshoots; statements on modern issues are mostly inferred at low confidence.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Kautsky argues production for sale must give way to production for use and that commodity production's contradictions grow; markets are the problem, not the solution.

public-ownership.rationale: The commentary states the aim as abolishing private ownership of the means of production and replacing production for sale with production by and for society.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Taxation of capital was an accepted social-democratic demand but Kautsky says reforms preserving private property are largely inoperative; support is real yet subordinate to expropriation.

unions-good.rationale: Kautsky calls the union movement the core of the militant proletariat and a school of organization and discipline, though he criticizes craft aristocracy.

property-fundamental.rationale: The program aims at abolishing private property in the means of production, so treating it as an inviolable right is rejected.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Kautsky sees trusts and syndicates as stages toward socialization rather than something to regulate back into competition; tighter regulation is accepted as a reform but not a goal.

cut-welfare.rationale: Labor legislation and social reform are supported as improving workers' condition; cutting them contradicts the program, although they are not seen as solving the root problem.

worker-ownership.rationale: Orthodox Marxists want social, not enterprise-level, ownership of production by society as a whole; worker ownership of firms is compatible in spirit but not the formula, so agree moderately.

strong-leader.rationale: Kautsky condemned rule by an elite or single will as undemocratic and counterposed mass democracy; the party stressed collective, majority decision.

state-harmful.rationale: Kautsky says the proletariat must conquer political power and transform the state rather than abolish it overnight; calling it harmful and unnecessary is far from his view.

limit-guns.rationale: No stated position; Marxists historically favored an armed people in principle but gun control as such was not an orthodox question.

decide-locally.rationale: Orthodox Marxism favored a centralized democratic republic and centrally conducted socialist production; local autonomy was not a principle.

rehabilitation.rationale: Crime was seen as a product of social conditions to be removed by socialism, implying rehabilitative over punitive approaches; the Erfurt text does not detail prisons.

traditional-family.rationale: Kautsky's commentary treats the family as historically changing form and discusses the 'abolition of the family' charge; he does not hold traditional structures to be foundational.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Kautsky's discussion of the family and woman's position treats sex roles as historically shaped by economic conditions, supporting a social-construction reading.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Kautsky says the proletarian is a citizen of the world and national prejudice fades; preservation of national tradition is not a goal.

gradual-change.rationale: Orthodoxy accepts parliamentary struggle but insists on social revolution replacing the property system; gradual respect for established institutions is rejected as revisionism.

free-trade.rationale: Marx-derived orthodoxy supported free trade as accelerating capitalist development without thinking it benefits everyone; adherents split with protectionist views, so neutral.

nation-first.rationale: Kautsky's text holds that proletarians are citizens of the world and the workers of all nations depend on one another.

open-borders.rationale: The proletarian's lack of a settled country and internationalism point to eventual open borders as an aim, though not a program demand.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Productive forces development is the engine of history for orthodox materialism, but social ownership rather than technology alone solves problems; qualified agreement.

revolution-justified.rationale: Kautsky says the aim is social revolution, conquest of political power by the proletariat, though revolution need not mean violence.

central-planning.rationale: Socialist production is conducted by and for society according to plan, replacing market anarchy; Kautsky still expected exchange of surpluses and some trade.

socialized-markets.rationale: Kautsky targets commodity production itself; markets even among social firms would continue the production for sale he wants superseded.

land-value-tax.rationale: Single-tax schemes are reform nostrums that leave capital in place; Kautsky calls most proposed reforms useless or injurious.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inheritance taxes were a standard social-democratic reform, supported as lesser measure while the real aim is abolishing property in means of production.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Kautsky says small production is doomed by economic development and socialism cannot preserve it, though it can help small producers as consumers.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The goal of ending commodity production and wage labor is core, but the sources give no timetable or treatment of money, so agreement is moderate.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Leaving money to the market contradicts replacing commodity production by social production; Kautsky wants social control of credit, not market money.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Kautsky's labor movement is class struggle by independent unions and party against the capitalist class, not state-sanctioned partnership.

one-party-rule.rationale: Kautsky denounces dictatorship as suppressing opposing views and criticizes Soviet exclusion of other socialist parties; he defends democracy and plural socialist parties.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Kautsky stresses universal suffrage and democratic republic as the working class's political terrain; hereditary rule is incompatible.

democracy-best.rationale: Kautsky holds that the proletarian class struggle presupposes democracy and that socialism must extend democracy into the economy.

direct-votes.rationale: The commentary discusses the future state's structure but my extract did not state a view on referendums; adherents like Bebel favored direct legislation yet others stressed parliament.

workers-councils.rationale: Kautsky opposed Soviet-style councils replacing parliament as the basis of power and defended the Commune only as pluralist and democratic.

right-to-secede.rationale: Orthodox socialists affirmed national self-determination in principle while preferring larger states and class unity; they were split.

natural-rulers.rationale: Kautsky rejects rule by an educated elite and sees democracy and mass organization as the foundation.

political-violence-never.rationale: Kautsky treats revolution as a possibility that need not involve violence, but he does not renounce force and condemns pacifist illusions.

war-builds-character.rationale: Kautsky presents militarism as a product of capitalist competition and celebrates May Day protests against war.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Orthodoxy rests on materialist science of society, which excludes scripture as basis for law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Orthodox Marxism views the state and law as instruments to be captured by the working class; privatizing them would be capitalist, so rejected.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The internationalist proletarian is a citizen of the world and national prejudice fades, so ethnic homogeneity is no goal.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Orthodox Marxism treats historical materialism and class struggle as the scientific key to history.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Socialist distribution aims at abolishing class distinctions, but Kautsky and the tradition gave work-based distribution first; qualified agreement.

civilizational-union.rationale: Workers' unity across borders is by class, not civilization or religion.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Kautsky says men act in their own interests (not puppets) as a fact, but the socialist ethic is solidarity and collective ownership.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Kautsky defends democratic rights and individual freedom against dictatorship, so rights are not subordinated to duties.

limit-population.rationale: Kautsky disputed Malthusian population explanations of poverty, attributing poverty to social institutions; active limiting is disfavored.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Orthodox Marxism views industrial capitalism as progressively developing the productive forces that make socialism possible.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Orthodox determinism held history cannot be hurried and institutions change when conditions mature; adherents welcomed technology but not disruption for its own sake.

restore-past-order.rationale: Orthodox Marxism is progressive: history moves forward to socialism and small production's past cannot be restored.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Lukács holds orthodoxy is commitment to a method and a total view, rejecting pragmatic eclecticism.

direct-action.rationale: Kautsky urges using universal suffrage and parliament along with union and party organization, not abandoning elections.

means-match-ends.rationale: Kautsky ties democracy as method to socialism's democratic aim, yet orthodoxy also stressed revolutionary conquest; split.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Kautsky discusses socialist production and the division of labor under capitalism; abolition as such is not his view, but classical Marx hinted at it, so mild disagreement.

production-for-use.rationale: Kautsky states directly that production for sale must be replaced by socialist production for and by society.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The Erfurt commentary's analysis of wages, profit and the proletariat treats profit as arising from workers' labor unpaid by capital; philanthropy cannot remove this.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Kautsky read the dictatorship of the proletariat as a condition of majority rule, not a form of government suppressing opponents, so he rejects dictatorial power over former rulers.

collective-farming.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale says socialism cannot preserve small farms and should persuade peasants into collectives; it rejects only coercion, which the statement does not require, so the sources cited here do not support this answer.

reviewHistory.rationale: Kautsky insists that socialism cannot preserve small farms but would not coerce peasants into collectives; the program emphasizes persuasion.

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its rationale says socialism cannot preserve small farms and should persuade peasants into collectives; it rejects only coercion, which the statement does not require, so the sources cited here do not support this answer.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Kautsky says capitalist competition fuels conflict between nations and militarism, though later he argued ultra-imperialism could avoid wars; hence moderate agreement.

taxation-theft.rationale: Orthodoxy aims at common ownership and conquering the state, treating taxation as normal state function.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Orthodoxy is class-based and treats property rights as historical class instruments; rights belonging only to individuals is rejected, though individual rights are defended against dictatorship.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Kautsky insists on democracy and the vote as the road to power; exit is an irrelevant check.

state-as-business.rationale: The proletariat is to conquer the state and use it for common ownership; running it as a business for customers is the capitalist approach.

positive-liberty.rationale: The commentary on socialism and freedom ties freedom to ending economic dependence of workers on owners.

media-academia-power.rationale: Kautsky stresses class power rooted in property, not universities or media; a free press matters to workers.

organic-representation.rationale: Kautsky holds that workers should organize in an independent labor party and use universal suffrage in parliament.

total-state.rationale: Kautsky defends democratic rights against dictatorial control of life; the total state is rejected.

national-rebirth.rationale: The movement's aim is class emancipation across nations, not national regeneration.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Kautsky blames capitalist competition for militarism and sees national rivalry as a capitalist contradiction.

bound-labor.rationale: Feudal bondage is a pre-capitalist stage of exploitation; socialism aims at free and equal individuals.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Orthodoxy claims historical materialism is a science, though Lukács notes bourgeois ideology shapes thought; the position is that science of society is possible.

single-common-good.rationale: Class interests are opposed under capitalism, so politics is class struggle rather than a single common good.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Kautsky says the decisive question is whether the proletariat can transfer democracy from politics to economics.

economic-freedom.rationale: Orthodoxy holds economic freedom under capitalism is domination by owners and political freedom rests on democratic action of workers.

rule-by-example.rationale: Kautsky bases politics on democratic mass struggle and law, not rulers' moral example.

national-self-determination.rationale: The Second International recognized national self-determination in principle, though Kautsky's text stresses internationalism.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Orthodox Marxism holds itself a scientific method of dialectical materialism; Lukács calls it the road to truth.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Workers of all nations depend on one another, so benefits should not exclude immigrant workers.

class-collaboration.rationale: Kautsky's account of the class struggle holds the proletariat must rely on its own efforts and dismisses cooperation via philanthropy.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Orthodoxy aims at inheriting culture and science for the working class, not destroying it.

workers-nation.rationale: Kautsky says the workers' movement is international in character and the proletarian is a citizen of the world.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The Erfurt tradition demanded women's equality; the commentary treats the dissolution of the proletarian family as a capitalist effect and rejects fixed roles.

ban-interest.rationale: Orthodoxy critiques commodity production and capital as a whole, not interest alone; banning interest on lending is a petty-bourgeois nostrum.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Kautsky says the modern state must be conquered by the working class and its economic significance is analyzed as a class instrument.

elite-replacement.rationale: Orthodox Marxists explained migration as labour-market movement under capitalism, which leaves no room for a replacement conspiracy.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Kautsky's commentary treats women's dependence and the family's dissolution under capitalism, but orthodoxy grounds women's subordination in class and property rather than in patriarchy itself; moderate agreement.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Orthodoxy criticized bourgeois politicians as class representatives, not generic corruption; split.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenic coercion contradicts the materialist emphasis on social causes.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The state is to be conquered and used for common ownership of production, far beyond a minimal state.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The commentary pictures socialism as free and equal individuals; classes are to be abolished.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Restrictions on conscience conflict with the democratic freedoms Kautsky demands.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Kautsky criticized strengthening state power over the democratic base in Russia; orthodoxy expected the state to be transformed, not enhanced.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Kautsky holds that a people is not ripe for socialism while the majority are hostile and the dictatorship of the proletariat means majority rule.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist aims serve capitalist rivalry that the tradition criticizes.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Kautsky does not renounce force in social revolution or the state's coercive capacity; absolute non-aggression is the libertarian position.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Capitalist competition develops the productive forces, but the program replaces competition with planned cooperation.

vanguard-party.rationale: Kautsky says socialism was brought to workers by bourgeois intellectuals who broke with their class and joined the party, but he did not demand a disciplined cadre vanguard, so agreement is partial.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The labor movement represents the wage-earning proletariat; the program prioritizes workers' needs, though in class rather than charitable terms.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Kautsky treats the union movement and strikes as core elements of working-class struggle.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The commentary attributes poverty to capitalist social institutions, not to population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Internationalist solidarity regards national and ethnic differences as fading prejudices.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Kautsky condemned suppression of opposition as dictatorship even by socialists.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Reform measures easing workers' conditions are supported, though Kautsky doubts they remove capitalism's contradictions.

party-controls-media.rationale: Kautsky argued against forcible suppression of the utterance of opponents.

party-commands-army.rationale: Subordinating the state forces to a party contradicts the democratic state Kautsky defended.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Lukács describes the party representing the movement as a whole, and the Social Democrats prided themselves on discipline.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Presidential command over forces conflicts with democratic parliamentary orientation.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Kautsky's text opposes war between capitalist states but the Second International mainstream backed national defense in 1914; the revolutionary-defeatist line is Lenin's, so the typical orthodox adherent disagrees.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Orthodox Marxists defended free press and expression as workers' needs.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Orthodoxy aims at social ownership of means of production, not at making every family a property owner.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Kautsky sees small farming doomed and the proletariat as the progressive class; romanticizing rural life is rejected.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Kautsky holds that scientific socialism came from educated bourgeois idealists who joined the workers, so he does not disparage the educated.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Orthodox progressivism of stages sat uneasily with relativism; adherents split.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Marxists regard political forms as resting on the economic basis, so political change without property change is insufficient.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Kautsky defended democratic means and universal suffrage, so an elected assembly is the appropriate means.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Orthodoxy holds private property in means of production is a historical form to be superseded by social ownership, closer to this than to absolute property rights.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Wikipedia notes that anti-revisionists call the Soviet and Chinese states state capitalist while others differ; Kautsky condemned Bolshevik rule but orthodox adherents are split.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Kautsky's democratic republic gives no stated view on a symbolic head of state; adherents would split.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Progressive taxation was a standard social-democratic reform; a flat rate favors the wealthy.

character-from-environment.rationale: Kautsky's treatment of the proletarian and capitalist classes holds that men's actions follow their social conditions.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Orthodoxy favors rule by the many through democracy, not mixed regimes.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody presumptions are a modern family-law question the Erfurt commentary never touches, so adherents are split.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Orthodoxy expected classes to disappear with socialism; the thesis that the struggle intensifies is Stalinist and Maoist.

land-redistribution.rationale: Kautsky says small farming cannot be preserved by socialism, hence transfer of land to small cultivators is not the orthodox program; split.

women-must-cover.rationale: Orthodox socialists supported women's equality; compulsory dress is rejected.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Unity is by class, not ancestry.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Austro-Marxists proposed it while Kautsky and others disagreed; split.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Orthodox socialists favored minorities' struggle for equal rights alongside the working class in their countries.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Wikipedia identifies historical materialism, with changing economic conditions as history's driver, as orthodoxy's core.

ban-cartels.rationale: Kautsky treats syndicates and trusts as stages in the growth of large production leading toward socialization, not something to break up.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Autarkic imperial blocs are products of capitalist rivalry and contradict internationalism.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: International labor standards fit internationalist labor legislation aims.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Wikipedia describes orthodoxy as deterministic: history cannot be hurried and revolution waits for ripe economic conditions.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Abolition of class privilege is core and the democratic program opposes hereditary rule.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Kautsky wants workers to help backward nations rise, not rule them.

patriotic-education.rationale: The proletarian is a citizen of the world and national prejudice fades.

public-money-creation.rationale: Social control of credit follows from social ownership; Kautsky discusses commerce and credit as part of capitalism to be socialized.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Orthodoxy held capitalism would collapse through internal contradictions and denounced Bernstein for denying it.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Imperial ambition is a capitalist feature.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Kautsky criticizes craft aristocracy of labor but sees workers as exploited; the imperialist-profit version is Leninist.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Orthodox socialists opposed colonial rule but had no doctrine on treaty validity; adherents would split.

elective-rulers.rationale: Kautsky insists on democracy and universal suffrage as the means to power.

minority-veto.rationale: Majority rule is central to Kautsky's democratic view.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Kautsky urges workers to use parliament and expects it to be transformed by proletarian participation.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Kautsky dismisses philanthropy as limited and says the proletariat must rely on itself.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Kautsky holds that every class struggle is political.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Frankfurt School theme rather than orthodox; Wikipedia places it among later Western Marxism.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Hegemony is Gramscian Western Marxism, not orthodox; orthodoxy stresses economic and state power.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Dependency theory is later; orthodoxy located exploitation chiefly within class relations.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Workers' solidarity favors help for backward nations.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Kautsky condemned Bolshevik dictatorship but orthodoxy never framed it as equivalence with fascism; split.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Orthodoxy treats stages of development as universal rather than civilizational.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Kautsky criticizes militarism and expects democratic politics.

filial-duty.rationale: The Erfurt commentary describes the changing, dissolving proletarian family but does not rule on duties of grown children.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Nationalist protectionism is not an orthodox aim.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Kautsky praises the Commune as a democratic proletarian regime; delegates bound and removable follow from it.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Individual market accounts contradict social provision and collective ownership.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Kautsky favors social ownership of production but his sources opened do not address use-based land tenure for individuals.

corporate-influence.rationale: The state as class instrument and capital's power over politics.

democratic-peace.rationale: Orthodoxy saw wars as capitalist rivalry regardless of regime form.

industrial-unions.rationale: Kautsky criticizes craft separation as aristocracy of labor and expects its erosion.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Kautsky discusses the so-called abolition of the family as a charge, but the sources do not favor ending legal marriage.

informal-organisation.rationale: Kautsky says a secret organisation cannot be democratic and urges a mass party.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Kautsky distinguishes private property in instruments of production from other property.

religion-illusion.rationale: Materialist outlook treats religion as ideological reflection of conditions; extent not sourced precisely.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Orthodoxy holds capitalism develops productive forces and prepares socialism.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Kautsky's discussion of proletarian family and woman's lot in capitalism ties women's condition to economics.

socialized-care.rationale: Bebel argued for it but Kautsky text does not.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Kautsky regards small cooperative utopian communities as utopian socialism, replaced by scientific socialism.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Orthodoxy holds socialism to be the only alternative.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Kautsky argues dictatorship suppresses opponents' utterance and democracy requires free debate.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Kautsky traces militarism to imperial competition and wants workers to help backward nations rise, not be governed for a metropole's gain.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Religious obligation to war contradicts materialism.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Orthodoxy's materialist science of society offers no basis for religious legitimacy and Kautsky's democratic path excludes armed removal of rulers on religious grounds.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Kautsky says the decisive question is transferring democracy from politics to economics.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Wikipedia says orthodoxy treated race as secondary; intersectionality is later.

alienated-labor.rationale: Alienation emphasized by Western Marxism; orthodox Kautskyan texts focus on exploitation.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Orthodoxy treated religion as private but did not address dress rules in state institutions.

social-market-economy.rationale: Kautsky says reforms preserving private property are inoperative in resolving contradictions.

property-franchise.rationale: Kautsky calls universal ballot a prerequisite of a healthy proletarian movement.

reification.rationale: Commodity fetishism is part of Marx's Capital which orthodoxy upholds, and Lukacs's essay on orthodoxy builds on it; Kautsky himself used it little.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Kautsky defended democracy and law against Bolshevik dictatorship and arbitrary rule by decree.

racial-franchise.rationale: The strand fought for universal suffrage and internationalism and denied that race divides workers.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Kautsky's Erfurt commentary describes capital concentrating in few hands and the propertied class dominating state and society; a Marxist reads this as domination of workers, though 'free society' is not the framing used.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The Erfurt Program rejects charity as a substitute for ending the proletariat's dependence and demands public social legislation and abolition of private ownership of production.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Kautsky's account of surplus value treats rent, interest and profit as unearned appropriation of workers' labour, a core part of the orthodox analysis.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Orthodox Marxism treats politics as class struggle grounded in material interests under historical materialism, not as a spiritual contest.

independent-unions.rationale: Kautsky treated unions as one arm of the class struggle alongside the party, separate from the state, though tied to the party in practice.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Kautsky defines the proletarian dictatorship as rule by the majority class through democracy, and criticised Bolshevik rule by a party elite.

municipal-property.rationale: Kautsky's commonwealth envisioned society-wide ownership organised nationally rather than by localities.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Orthodox Marxism rests on dialectical-materialist method and historical materialism as science.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Kautsky's Erfurt commentary puts class struggle and internationalism above any other group division.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Kautsky's commentary attacks militarism and the Second International accepted only defensive wars.

capital-controls.rationale: Orthodoxy aimed at abolishing private ownership outright instead of regulating capital flows, so adherents would not endorse nor firmly oppose this reform.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Kautsky's Erfurt Program commentary makes trade unions and collective struggle over wages and hours a core part of the workers' fight.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Kautsky's Dictatorship of the Proletariat argues that the proletariat should win the existing democratic state through universal suffrage and parliament, and he rejected the Bolshevik destruction of democratic institutions.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Orthodoxy holds that socialism needs one planned, socially owned mode of production (production for use), so a fixed system is expected rather than free experiment.

sacred-nation.rationale: Orthodox Marxism is materialist and treats the nation as a historical class-bound formation, with the working class internationalist, so a sacred nation is rejected.

workers-own-party.rationale: Orthodox Marxism centred on an independent mass workers' party, as the SPD was, that fights the class struggle apart from bourgeois parties.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The Erfurt Program demanded that religion be declared a private matter and the church separated from the state, which rules out legal precedence for any interpretation.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Kautsky held democracy to be the rule of the majority and the ground of proletarian struggle, but treated it as tied to class content, not merely to elections.

women-suffrage.rationale: The Erfurt Program demanded universal, equal suffrage without distinction of sex, and the SPD championed women's voting rights.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Orthodoxy traced women's subjection mainly to property relations and the family under private ownership, with religion secondary; adherents are split.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Kautsky's commonwealth abolishes private ownership of the means of production, and first-claim title to resources runs against that.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Orthodox Marxism treats historical materialism as science and religion as a private matter in the Erfurt programme, so inerrant scripture is rejected.

national-church-status.rationale: The Erfurt programme demands that religion be declared a private matter and the separation of church and state.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Kautsky insisted on democracy and legality and condemned Bolshevik terror, so killing suspects without trial would be incompatible with his position.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Kautsky makes the mass party, trade unions and parliament the instruments of the working class, so a leader bypassing them is contrary to his strategy.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Kautsky's critique holds that voluntary wage contracts under private ownership still produce exploitation, so a fair process does not justify the outcome.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: The labour theory of value is part of the Marxist economics Kautsky systematised and which orthodoxy defended against revisionist critics.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Kautsky was internationalist but the pre-1914 SPD also mixed defence of the homeland with class politics; the sources do not settle it.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Kautsky's commonwealth replaces commodity production with production for use, and he opposed single-party dictatorship, so both halves of the statement conflict with his view.

missingStatements.text: Capitalism will collapse through its own internal contradictions.
missingStatements.rationale: Collapse theory is the orthodox doctrine that Kautsky held and Bernstein's revisionism denied.

missingStatements.text: Socialism cannot be reached before capitalism has developed the economic conditions for it.
missingStatements.rationale: Plekhanov and the Mensheviks argued Russia had to pass through a capitalist stage, and orthodoxy held history cannot be hurried.

missingStatements.text: Socialists should use universal suffrage and parliament to win political power for the working class.
missingStatements.rationale: Kautsky calls the universal ballot a prerequisite of a healthy proletarian movement and urges workers to use parliament.

missingStatements.text: Reforms that leave private ownership of the means of production in place cannot remove capitalism's contradictions.
missingStatements.rationale: Kautsky pronounces such reforms inoperative against the growing contradictions, and orthodoxy attacked Bernstein's reformism.

notes: Kautsky's line is contested within the tradition: Lukacs makes orthodoxy a matter of method rather than theses, Leninists claimed the mantle while rejecting Kautsky, and impossibilists reject reformism. Answers follow Kautsky's mainstream Second International position.
